description: An electric lap steel: eight modelled strings stopped by one rigid steel bar rather than by frets, so moving the bar moves every string by the same ratio

params.text: Sets where the bar lies across the neck; with a cable in the bar position jack it becomes a transposition in key on top of that instead
Angles the bar across the eight strings, up to six semitones of tilt, which is how one tuning gives major, minor and dominant voicings
Sets how fast the bar travels, as a rate rather than a time, so a wide move takes proportionally longer than a narrow one
Sets how far the bar rocks either side of the pitch
Sets how long a string rings, 0.2 to 20 seconds
Sets how quickly the high partials die away
Sets how hard the strings are picked
Sets where the pickup is placed, 4 to 34 per cent of the way from the bridge
Sets where the pickup's coil resonance peaks, 1.6kHz to 6.2kHz
Drives the amplifier harder
Transposes the whole instrument in semitones
Transposes the whole instrument in octaves
Picks which of sixteen fingerpicking rolls the auto-player uses
Sets how many of the roll's notes are played
Runs the roll
Returns the roll to its start on each press
Sets how much the strings that are not being played are damped by the hand resting on them
Sets the volume pedal's level after the pick attack, per note
Sets how much a ringing string sets its neighbours going through the shared bridge
Sets how fast the bar rocks, 2Hz to 9Hz
Sets how much the picking varies: the accent on the struck note first, then the note-to-note jitter
Picks the scale the bar position is snapped to, or leaves it free at the first position

inputs.text: Places the bar as a volt per octave; with a cable here the position knob becomes a transposition in key on top of it
Changes the bar's tilt, ±5V added to the slant knob
Changes the ring time, ±5V added to the decay knob
Changes how fast the high partials die, ±5V added to the damping knob
Changes the pick hardness, ±5V added to the pick knob
Changes the coil resonance, ±5V added to the tone knob
Transposes the whole instrument as a volt per octave, or, on the menu setting, places the bar and picks the string at once
A rise picks a string: one polyphonic channel per string, or every string at once from a single-channel cable
Sets each string's velocity, 0-10V, one polyphonic channel per string
Each rise advances the roll by one step
Sweeps through all sixteen rolls, ±5V added to the roll knob
Changes how many of the roll's notes are played, ±5V added to the density knob
The volume pedal, 0-10V, which replaces the swell knob; the menu can make it a bipolar offset on the knob instead
Transposes the instrument, a volt per octave snapped to semitones, added to the root knob
Picks the scale, one volt per scale, with 0V leaving the bar free

outputs.text: The left side of the eight strings mixed
The right side of the eight strings mixed
The even-numbered strings summed on their own
The odd-numbered strings summed on their own

notes: the pickup is fixed in space while the speaking length of the string changes, so its position as a fraction of the string climbs as the bar goes up the neck and the tone hollows out with it
the display is playable: the strings are strummed with the mouse, and each string's own settings are edited there rather than on a control
placing a SLIDE XP immediately to the right gives each string its own gate, velocity and audio jack
menu: Auto roll moves the bar — lets the roll move the bar as it plays rather than picking against a bar you have placed
Tuning — a submenu of lap steel tunings for the eight strings
V/oct: Transposes the whole instrument, Places the bar and picks the string — chooses what the pitch input does
Pickup: Modern single coil, Horseshoe (bark and midrange honk) — picks which pickup the strings are heard through
Mouse: Hover strums the strings, Click and drag only — chooses whether moving the pointer across the strings plays them or a button has to be held
VOL offsets the swell (for bipolar CV) — makes the volume pedal jack add to the swell knob rather than replace it, so a bipolar CV can be used
Hover plays when Rack is in the background — lets the pointer play the strings while another application is in front; off by default, since hover events keep arriving
